channel.title: Said & Checked: Michigan — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day from or about Michigan, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Michigan, 2026-11-24: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Bill Huizenga)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Bill Huizenga, U.S. Representative from Michigan: “she was, and is, a spy” Unsettled. No U.S. government body was found to have officially identified Alice Huang as a spy, and none has said she is not one; the Nov. 16 Commerce and Justice Department statement describes an open criminal export-control investigation of Megaspeed and does not mention espionage. AskAmerica's screening-list data shows three Megaspeed companies (Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand) on the Commerce Entity List and no entry for her as an individual.

item.title: Said & Checked, Michigan, 2026-11-23: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Chris Van Hollen)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Chris Van Hollen, U.S. Senator from Maryland: “Our current leader, Senator Schumer, sided with crypto and AIPAC to try to defeat him as well as to try to defeat our new senator, Senator Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota.” Unsettled. Schumer endorsed Rep. Haley Stevens against El-Sayed in Michigan, and AskAmerica's FEC data show AIPAC's United Democracy Project spending about $20.8 million against El-Sayed. No record was found of a Schumer role against Flanagan in Minnesota, of crypto-industry PAC spending in either race, or of AIPAC spending against Flanagan.

item.title: Said & Checked, Michigan, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 3 unsettled (Tim Walberg)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Tim Walberg, U.S. Representative from Michigan: “Fishing in the Great Lakes alone contributes more than $5 billion to the regional economy and supports over 75,000 jobs.” Unsettled. A Great Lakes Fishery Commission study puts recreational fishing's economic output at $5.1 billion (reported by Michigan Public), matching the dollar figure. The commission's factsheet reportedly counts about 35,800 recreational and nearly 3,000 commercial jobs, about 39,000 in all, short of 75,000; that factsheet could not be read directly, so the jobs figure is not settled here.
  • Tim Walberg, U.S. Representative from Michigan: “The Great Lakes are home to the largest breeding population of cormorants in the United States, with over 70 percent of the population nesting in the Great Lakes alone.” Unsettled. USGS's 1999 survey puts 68% of North American nesting double-crested cormorants in the Interior region, which spans Ontario and several U.S. states and is not a Great Lakes share. No survey found reports the Great Lakes' share of the U.S. breeding population.
  • Tim Walberg, U.S. Representative from Michigan: “Populations of double-crested cormorants are exploding in regions across the country, and in some cases doubling every 4 years.” Unsettled. USGS reported 22% annual growth in Ontario and the Great Lakes states in the early 1990s, about a doubling every 3.5 years. But the 2022 Fish and Wildlife Service report says the Great Lakes population 'may be stable or declining' and that regional monitoring stopped after 2018, so current rapid growth is not shown.

item.title: Said & Checked, Michigan, 2026-11-15: none false or contradicted, 4 unsettled (John Moolenaar)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • John Moolenaar, U.S. Representative from Michigan: “Yes, he has. And also representatives from Nvidia. We are in the process of discussing exact dates.” Unsettled. ABC News reported around Nov. 10 that Jensen Huang and Nvidia had not responded to the committee chairs' request for a closed-door briefing on Nov. 18. That predates the statement, so it neither confirms nor rules out a later agreement; no confirmation or refusal by the committee or the company was found.
  • John Moolenaar, U.S. Representative from Michigan: “she's a Chinese national, set up a company that has been able to access over $12 billion of high-end chips. And there's an investigation as to whether those chips were illegally smuggled into China.” Unsettled. CNBC reports, citing Bloomberg, that the U.S. government is investigating whether the company moved Nvidia chips to China, which fits the second part. The "over $12 billion" figure was not found in any official or company record: the pages read give about $2 billion in purchases and $7.5 billion in related imports.
  • John Moolenaar, U.S. Representative from Michigan: “So, anyone who doesn't comply with the CCP can be imprisoned, they or their family members.” Unsettled. The law, as quoted by Wikipedia, requires cooperation with intelligence work, but commentary cited there says it has no enforcement mechanism. No page read documents a person or a relative imprisoned for refusing to cooperate, and "anyone" is loose wording.
